title: arxiv_2505.03445v1
universal_lens: Neural Distance Fields (NDF) encode pose manifolds; polar coordinates decouple angular and radial errors for refined 2D HPE under domain shifts. The projection of a rigid 3D kinematic tree onto a 2D imaging plane induces a continuous, non-linear manifold deformation. This primitive formalizes the resulting topological distortion as a neural distance field, mapping arbitrary 2D joint configurations to their geodesic distance from the valid pose subspace, unifying angular and radial geometric constraints.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on NDF-manifold embeddings enables conformal uncertainty quantification of pose estimates, supporting robust GSI analytics across sports domains. In GSI, the 2D NDF acts as a conformal anomaly detector for tracking systems. By treating erroneous pose estimations as out-of-distribution samples, the gradient of the distance field provides a Bayesian posterior correction, refining noisy sensor data into high-confidence kinematic states without explicit 3D reconstruction.
gse_mapping: Situation-aware state transitions in GSE utilize NDF-driven pose corrections to maintain dynamic consistency during athletic motion analysis. GSE utilizes this primitive for real-time situational reasoning. The learned prior defines the valid state-transition boundaries for player movement. When an estimated pose violates the NDF threshold, the engine triggers a state rollback or interpolation, ensuring physical plausibility in dynamic sports simulations.

primitives.name: Pose Prior Refinement via Neural Distance Fields
primitives.verbatim_quote: To address these limitations, we propose a 2D pose prior-guided refinement approach based on Neural Distance Fields (NDF).
primitives.assumptions: The pose prior manifold is learnable via NDF; refinement iteratively minimizes distance to embedded pose space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When motion blur or occlusion causes invalid pose estimates, NDF-based correction fails without sufficient training data.

layer2.mapping: NDF encodes real pose manifold; backpropagation corrects fake poses by minimizing embedded distance to manifold.
layer2.telemetry: Pose correction accuracy measured via L2 distance between corrected and ground-truth poses.

primitives.name: Polar Coordinate-Based Pose Representation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Unlike existing approaches that rely solely on angular representations of human poses, we introduce a polar coordinate-based representation that explicitly incorporates joint connection lengths, enabling a more accurate correction of erroneous pose estimations.
primitives.assumptions: Joint distances and angles are separable in polar space; geometric structure improves error localization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In cases of severe occlusion or extreme limb articulation, polar decomposition may lose discriminative power.

layer2.mapping: Polar coordinates separate angular and radial components, improving kernel alignment in pose correction.
layer2.telemetry: Angular vs radial error reduction compared to Cartesian representations via cross-validation.

primitives.name: Non-Geodesic Distance Metric for Pose Correction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Additionally, we define a novel non-geodesic distance metric that separates angular and radial discrepancies, which we demonstrate is better suited for polar representations than traditional geodesic distances.
primitives.assumptions: Separation of angular and radial errors allows independent optimization; non-geodesic metric aligns with polar geometry.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Metric becomes less effective when angular and radial errors are highly correlated or when pose variation exceeds training distribution.

layer2.mapping: Separate angular and radial metrics enable targeted refinement in polar pose space.
layer2.telemetry: Improvement in pose plausibility score over standard geodesic distance in synthetic and real-world datasets.

primitives.name: Gradient-Based Batch Projection Augmentation
primitives.verbatim_quote: To mitigate data scarcity, we develop a gradient-based batch-projection augmentation strategy, which synthesizes realistic pose samples through iterative refinement.
primitives.assumptions: Iterative gradient descent in latent space generates plausible synthetic poses; augmentation preserves pose topology.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Synthetic samples degrade when training data distribution is too sparse or misaligned with real-world variability.

layer2.mapping: Batch projection mimics real pose generation via gradient ascent in NDF embedding space.
layer2.telemetry: Augmented dataset size and generalization performance on unseen sports domains.

primitives.name: Neural Distance Field 2D Pose Prior
primitives.verbatim_quote: To the best of our knowledge, the only existing work that models 2D human pose priors is POST [21], which employs a NDF.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: f_ndf: Neural distance field operator (dimensionless); X: 2D pose configuration space (dimensionless coordinates); Y: Predicted geodesic distance to the valid pose manifold (dimensionless metric).
primitives.assumptions: The valid 2D poses form a low-dimensional, continuous submanifold within the high-dimensional joint coordinate space; the distance to this manifold is differentiable almost everywhere.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur when joint projections overlap completely (radial length approaches zero), causing undefined angular derivatives, or when extreme occlusions place the input entirely outside the convex hull of the training distribution.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the GSI Conformal Anomaly Detector. The NDF output Y maps directly to the conformal score used to evaluate if a new observation belongs to the reference set of valid athletic postures.
layer2.telemetry: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of refined 2D joint positions against ground truth annotations on held-out video clips.

primitives.name: Polar Coordinate Joint Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: Moreover, unlike 3D poses where joint connection lengths are fixed, 2D joint lengths vary continuously from zero to their full projected length, introducing additional variability.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: v_i: Feature vector for joint i (dimensionless); \theta^{(1)}_i, \theta^{(2)}_i: Normalized angular components representing direction (dimensionless unit vector); r_i: Radial component representing projected limb length (pixels/meters).
primitives.assumptions: Limb connectivity is preserved; the projection of a 3D limb can be accurately decomposed into a directional unit vector and a scalar magnitude in 2D space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The polar representation becomes ill-conditioned when r_i -> 0, as the angular components \theta become mathematically undefined, leading to gradient explosions during backpropagation.

layer2.mapping: Maps to the GSE State-Vector Kernel. The polar decomposition isolates rotational dynamics (angles) from translational scaling (radius), allowing independent modeling of player orientation and stride length.
layer2.telemetry: Variance reduction in predicted joint angles compared to raw Cartesian coordinate inputs under heavy perspective distortion.

primitives.name: Hierarchical Encoder-Decoder NDF
primitives.verbatim_quote: Pose-NDF [24] models 3D human poses using a Neural Distance Field (NDF) [5], while H-NeRF [26] learns 3D pose priors using Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) [18].
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: f_ndf: Composite distance function; g_enc: Hierarchical encoder network mapping pose X to latent feature Z \in \mathbb{R}^{J \cdot L}; g_dec: Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) decoder mapping Z to distance Y.
primitives.assumptions: The complex topology of the 2D pose manifold can be compressed into a lower-dimensional latent space Z without losing critical geometric boundary information.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the latent dimension J*L is insufficient to capture the multi-modal nature of extreme athletic poses, resulting in over-smoothed distance fields that blur distinct kinematic clusters.

layer2.mapping: Directly isomorphic to the GSI Latent Manifold Learner. The encoder extracts invariant features from noisy tracking data, while the decoder reconstructs the probability density of valid states.
layer2.telemetry: Reconstruction loss (L2) between true distances and predicted distances on a validation set of synthetic and real poses.

primitives.name: Gradient-Based Pose Synthesis
primitives.verbatim_quote: • We introduce a gradient-based data augmentation method that synthesizes new pose samples during training.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D: Training dataset; x: Pose sample (real x_gt or fake x_fk); d: Ground truth distance to the manifold (0 for real, >0 for fake); N: Total number of samples.
primitives.assumptions: The gradient of the distance field with respect to the input pose coordinates points towards the nearest valid pose on the manifold, enabling the generation of realistic 'fake' negative samples.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Optimization diverges if the learning rate is too high, causing synthesized poses to escape the local basin of attraction and generate physically impossible configurations.

layer2.mapping: Corresponds to the GSE Adversarial Stress-Test Generator. It actively probes the boundaries of the valid state space to harden the model against rare but plausible edge-case movements.
layer2.telemetry: Improvement in robustness metrics (e.g., PCKh) when evaluating the model on out-of-distribution viewpoints or heavily occluded sequences.

reasoning_traces.think: The fundamental challenge addressed in this chapter window is the severe ambiguity inherent in projecting a rigid, constrained 3D kinematic tree onto a 2D imaging plane. In 3D space, skeletal constraints—such as fixed bone lengths and limited joint rotation ranges—define a highly structured, low-dimensional manifold. However, the perspective projection collapses depth information, causing a single valid 3D pose to map to a vast continuum of 2D configurations depending on the camera's extrinsic parameters. Furthermore, the apparent lengths of limbs in 2D vary continuously from their maximum 3D length down to zero (when aligned with the optical axis), destroying the fixed-distance priors that simplify 3D modeling. To overcome this, the authors pivot from traditional Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), which often struggle with the fine-grained geometric details required for 2D refinement, to Neural Distance Fields (NDFs). An NDF treats the space of all possible 2D joint configurations as a metric space and learns a scalar field representing the shortest distance from any given point to the surface of the valid pose manifold. By parameterizing joints in polar coordinates—separating angular orientation from radial projection—the model explicitly accounts for the continuous variability of 2D joint lengths. The core mathematical innovation lies in formulating the prior as a differentiable function $f_{\text{ndf}}$, implemented via a hierarchical encoder-decoder architecture. This allows the system not only to classify a pose as valid or invalid but also to compute gradients that guide erroneous estimates back onto the manifold. The introduction of gradient-based data augmentation further solidifies this approach; by optimizing fake samples to lie at specific distances from the manifold, the network learns a robust decision boundary even from sparse video data. This transforms the problem of pose refinement from a heuristic smoothing task into a rigorous geometric optimization over a learned Riemannian manifold.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive emerges from the convergence of computer vision's shape analysis and deep learning's implicit representations. Historically, pose estimation relied on parametric models (e.g., SMPL) or probabilistic graphical models. The shift toward VAEs (like VPose) introduced latent space regularization, but often at the cost of spatial fidelity. The advent of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) in 3D reconstruction demonstrated the power of implicit fields for capturing complex geometry. This work retroactively applies these 3D geometric insights to the 2D domain, recognizing that 2D poses, despite their ambiguity, still reside on a learnable manifold. It bridges the gap between classical kinematic constraints and modern differentiable rendering techniques.

It does not merely memorize pixel patterns; it infers the underlying physical intent and structural validity of a posture. When observing a fragmented or noisy 2D skeleton (perhaps due to occlusion or motion blur), the 'mind' of the NDF queries its internal geometric database: 'Does this arrangement of angles and radii correspond to a physically possible human state?' If the answer is no, it calculates the minimal adjustment required to restore plausibility. This mirrors how a coach or opponent intuitively predicts an athlete's next move based on subtle shifts in body alignment, effectively modeling the agent's physical constraints and capabilities rather than just their visual appearance.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises if the learned NDF manifold becomes overly smooth or disconnected. If the encoder compresses the pose data too aggressively (low J*L), distinct but valid athletic stances might collapse into a single latent region, causing the distance field to incorrectly penalize legitimate extreme poses. Additionally, leakage occurs if the gradient-based augmentation generates 'fake' poses that are actually valid but rare, confusing the boundary definition. Therefore, the system must enforce a strict anti-collinearity check: the gradient of the distance field must consistently point outward from the manifold core. If the gradient norm vanishes in regions known to contain valid poses (e.g., deep squats), the primitive must trigger a re-training cycle with higher-resolution polar embeddings to prevent systematic bias against specific movement domains.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 4 explores the application of a polar coordinate-based neural distance field (NDF) for 2D pose correction. The core innovation lies in representing pose data in polar space, which naturally captures rotational invariance and spatial continuity. The NDF learns a probabilistic distribution over valid poses, enabling refinement of raw pose estimates from various detectors such as AlphaPose, HRNet, and ViTPose. A key contribution is the introduction of a gradient loss term that enforces smoothness in the learned NDF, ensuring that nearby poses are consistent in their spatial derivatives. Additionally, a novel batch projection augmentation technique is introduced to enhance training efficiency, especially when data is limited. This method generates synthetic pose samples by projecting existing ones along gradient directions, effectively increasing dataset diversity without requiring additional annotations. The paper demonstrates that these techniques lead to consistent improvements in pose accuracy across multiple evaluation metrics (PCK@0.05, PCK@0.1, PCK@0.2), even when trained on reduced datasets. The ablation studies confirm that each component—polar representation, gradient loss, and batch projection—plays a critical role in achieving superior performance. These findings suggest that polar NDFs can serve as a universal prior for pose estimation tasks, offering both theoretical elegance and practical utility in real-world applications where pose accuracy is paramount.
